facts.population: Edentulous arches with 4 or more implants, in vitro models and patients (22 in vitro, 1 clinical study)
facts.intervention: Five categories of complete arch implant intraoral scan techniques (IOS-O, IOS-SA, IOS-CHS, IOS-CISP, IOS-IPG)
facts.comparison: Conventional abutment-level splinted open tray impression
facts.main_result: IOS-O and IOS-SA were more accurate than conventional for short spans but conventional was more accurate for long spans; IOS-CISP appeared better in long spans (limited evidence).
facts.funding_coi: No competing interests declared; work of AAFP Research in Fixed Prosthodontics Committee A
facts.limitations: Evidence for IOS-CISP is limited and studies on IOS-CHS and IOS-IPG are insufficient; nearly all studies in vitro.
facts.key_finding: In this systematic review of 23 mostly in vitro studies, intraoral scans (with or without scan aids) were more accurate than splinted open-tray impressions for short implant spans but less accurate for long spans. Calibrated scan protocols (IOS-CISP) looked better in long spans, but evidence is scant.
facts.clinical_bottom_line: For long-span complete arch implant records, the conventional splinted open-tray technique remains more reliable than standard intraoral scanning.
